diff.errorHint: git diff did not return normally. Retry, or inspect the file in a terminal.
diff.noFile: No line-level changes for this file (a mode change, or not yet tracked by git).
diff.truncatedBanner: This file is too large and was truncated; click "Load full diff" to see everything.

binary.title: Binary file
binary.hint: Binary files have no line-level diff; copy the patch or compare with a dedicated tool.

selection.hint: Click a line number to select that line; hold Shift to select a range.
selection.shortcuts: Shortcuts: s stage · u unstage · d discard
selection.truncatedHint: This file was truncated: load the full diff before staging lines.

diff.sheetDescription: Line-level diff view for the file

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: Recent application logs (generated locally, never uploaded, sanitized). Copy from here when reporting a problem.
logs.sanitizedNotice: Tokens and passwords are stripped before anything is written.
logs.highlighted: {{count}} line(s) near this error are highlighted.
logs.emptyHint: Log entries appear here once the app has been running for a while.
logs.errorHint: The log file may be unreachable. Retry, or open the log directory directly.

credentials.title: Saved credentials
credentials.description: Tokens and passwords live in the system credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Linux Secret Service). The list shows identifiers only; ciphertext never travels back to the UI.
credentials.keyringUnavailable: The system credential store is unavailable, so credentials cannot be saved securely. Reason
credentials.empty: No credentials saved yet. Add an access token here when you need to reach a private repository.
credentials.secretHint: The plaintext goes straight into the system credential store; it never appears in logs, audit records or this screen.
credentials.deleteImpact: The ciphertext is removed from the system credential store, so later network operations will ask for it again. The remote repository and anything already pushed are unaffected.
credentials.todoT44: Still to come (T4.4): signing in with GitHub (OAuth device flow), switching between accounts and syncing your profile. This version expects a pasted access token.

vault.createDescription: The passphrase derives the encryption key (Argon2id + AES-256-GCM) and the vault file lives in the app data directory. Unlike the system credential store, anyone who can read that file can attack the passphrase offline, so make it long.
vault.unlockDescription: Credentials are kept in an encrypted file; enter the passphrase to unlock them for synchronisation.
vault.forgotWarning: The passphrase is never stored: forgetting it means the credentials inside cannot be recovered (delete the vault and add them again).

ssh.title: SSH keys
ssh.description: Local keys and the current state of ssh-agent, for chasing down "Permission denied (publickey)". Only file names and public keys are read; private keys are never opened.
ssh.noDirectory: No ~/.ssh directory found (SSH may never have been set up here).
ssh.unavailable: Could not take inventory of the local SSH setup: reading the key directory failed, see the logs for details.
ssh.empty: No SSH keys yet. Generate one with ssh-keygen and add the public key to your hosting platform.
ssh.privateOnlyHint: No matching .pub file: regenerate it from the private key with ssh-keygen -y -f <private key path>.

agent.title: ssh-agent
agent.noIdentities: The agent is running but has no keys loaded
agent.noIdentitiesHint: Add one and retry: ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519. The agent takes precedence over the files, which is the usual source of confusion.
agent.notRunningHint: Start the agent and load a key first (on Windows this is usually the ssh-agent service being stopped).
agent.unknown: Could not determine the agent state

test.title: Test connection (remote URL)
test.hint: Runs a single git ls-remote: nothing local changes and nothing is written to the remote.

general.densityHint: Compact tightens list and page padding - useful on small screens or to fit more on one screen.
general.storageHint: Settings and repository records live in a SQLite database in the app data directory and survive restarts.
general.watchHint: Watch the repository directory so the app follows changes made in a terminal or editor. When this is off, the app polls every 15 seconds instead.
general.watchDebounceHint: Multiple file changes within this window collapse into a single refresh. Larger is calmer, smaller feels snappier.
general.perfHint: For large repositories with many changed files, trim rendering details automatically: char-level diff highlighting off, fewer diff context lines, and half the history page size. Forced off keeps every detail on large repositories.
general.themeNote: The theme is kept in browser local storage because it must be readable synchronously before the first paint; storing it in the database would cause a flash on startup.
general.loadFailedHint: The local database may be unreachable. Retry, and if it keeps failing check the logs.

advanced.logsPolicy: Logs are written to the app data directory, rotate on both a daily and a 10MB threshold, and are kept for 7 days. Tokens and passwords are stripped before writing, and nothing is ever uploaded.

appearance.themeHint: Applies immediately and is remembered; System follows the OS appearance.
appearance.languageHint: Text updates immediately (M0 already covers the shell and skeleton pages).

audit.title: Operation history
audit.hint: Every write operation (staging, committing, restoring, pruning…) leaves a record: time, result, duration and the linked snapshot. Everything stays on this machine.
audit.loadFailed: Could not read the operation history
audit.loadFailedHint: The local database may be unreachable. Retry.
audit.empty: No records yet. Stage or commit something and it will show up here.

retention.hint: Records beyond either limit are pruned automatically at startup; pruning is itself recorded.

snapshots.title: Snapshots and rollback
snapshots.description: A snapshot is taken automatically before each commit; go back to that point when something goes wrong.
snapshots.emptyHint: After the first commit, a "pre-commit" snapshot appears here.
snapshots.restoreConfirmDescription: This returns to the state where HEAD was {{oid}}.
snapshots.impactUnknown: The difference between the current state and the snapshot could not be read. Close and retry.
snapshots.impactRefMissing: This snapshot's anchor is gone; it cannot be restored.
snapshots.impactUnchanged: The working tree, index and HEAD already match the snapshot; nothing to restore.
snapshots.impactHead: HEAD will move from {{current}} back to {{oid}}.
snapshots.impactIndex: The index will also be restored to the snapshot's tree; staged but uncommitted content will be dropped.
snapshots.impactUntracked: Untracked files are neither deleted nor restored (only their paths were recorded).

commit.title: Commit
commit.description: Write the message, then check the exact git command in the preview.
commit.messagePlaceholder: Summarise the change (first line is the subject, keep it under ~72 chars)
commit.bodyPlaceholder: Optional details: why this changed and what it affects
commit.warningSubjectTooLong: The first line is long (keep it under ~{{max}} chars); it will be truncated in lists.
commit.amendHint: Fold the current content into the last commit and replace its message.
commit.signOffHint: Append a Signed-off-by line (required by DCO workflows).
commit.noVerifyHint: Do not run pre-commit / commit-msg and friends. Only tick this when you know the consequences.
commit.recentEmpty: This repository has no commits yet.
commit.stagedNoneHint: A commit contains only what is staged. Stage files or lines in the working tree first.
commit.previewDescription: This is exactly what will happen; it runs as soon as you confirm.
commit.previewHooksEmpty: This repository has no runnable commit hooks
commit.previewSnapshot: No snapshot will be created (snapshots land in M3). The current safety net is the plan preview plus the index fingerprint check.
commit.previewAmend: This rewrites the last commit; if it is already pushed, pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendEmpty: This repository has no commits yet, so there is nothing to amend.
commit.amendPushedWarning: This commit may already exist on a remote ({{refs}}). Rewriting it diverges local from remote; pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendPushedUnknown: This commit may already exist on a remote. Rewriting it diverges local from remote; pushing later needs force-with-lease.
commit.amendModeIncludeHint: Fold the staged content into the last commit (the git default).
commit.amendModeMessageOnlyHint: Replace the message only; staged content stays in the index and is not committed.
commit.hooksPhaseCodeCheck: Looks like a code check (the usual pre-commit shape)
commit.hooksPhaseMessageCheck: Looks like a commit-message check (the commit-msg stage)
commit.hooksPhaseDependencies: Looks like a dependency installation failure
commit.hooksPhaseUnknown: The output does not say which hook failed
commit.hooksListEmpty: This repository has no hooks installed.
commit.hooksListNotExecutable: Missing the execute bit, so git ignores it

clean.title: Working tree is clean
clean.hint: No uncommitted changes; edit files or pull and they will show up here.

error.title: Could not read the working tree status
error.hint: The repository may be unreachable. Retry, or reopen the repository.

workspace.largeChange: A large number of files changed (for example a branch switch); the list was refreshed.

discard.title: Discard these changes?
discard.description: The following changes will be lost and cannot be restored by this app:
discard.linesDescription: The selected lines in this file will be reverted. Staged content is not affected.

branches.title: Branches & tags
branches.createHint: Create a new branch from the current HEAD.
branches.deleteMergedHint: This branch is merged; its commits remain reachable from history.
branches.deleteUnmergedWarning: This branch has {{ahead}} commits of its own; force-deleting makes them unreachable (a snapshot is taken first):
branches.switchHint: The working tree has uncommitted changes; choose what to do with them:
branches.switchStash: Stash changes and restore after switching (recommended)
branches.switchForce: Discard all uncommitted changes (irreversible; a snapshot is taken first)
branches.tagHint: Leave the message empty for a lightweight tag; fill it for an annotated one.
branches.error: Failed to load branches and tags
branches.quickCreate: Type a name; Enter creates and switches

sync.fetchHint: Updates remote-tracking refs only; the local branch and worktree stay untouched
sync.pullHint: Fetches the upstream and merges it into the current branch (a snapshot is taken first)
sync.pushHint: Pushes the current branch to its upstream
sync.noUpstream: This branch has no upstream yet
sync.aheadTip: Commits this branch is ahead of upstream
sync.behindTip: Commits this branch is behind upstream

conflict.title: The pull produced conflicts
conflict.impact: The repository is left in a conflicted merge state: every conflicted file must be resolved before you can commit or push again. A snapshot was taken before this pull, so you can always roll back.

rejected.title: Push rejected
rejected.impact: The remote has commits you do not have. Fetching first is the safe path; if you must overwrite, use force-with-lease (git only overwrites when the remote still points at the commit you last saw).

lease.title: Overwrite the remote?
lease.impact: This comparison was just fetched: this branch is {{ahead}} commits ahead and {{behind}} commits behind. Overwriting rewrites the remote branch to your local history, so the commits you are behind will not be on it (they remain recoverable on the hosting platform).
lease.description: The latest state of {{upstream}} was fetched; this comparison is what the overwrite is based on.

stash.title: Stashes
stash.nothingToStash: Nothing to stash: the worktree is clean.
stash.untrackedFiles: Untracked files (stored separately in the third parent)
stash.conflict: Applying the stash produced {{count}} conflicts: the repository is in a conflicted state.
stash.emptyHint: When changes should be neither committed nor lost, stash them and take them back any time.
stash.dropImpact: The stash disappears from this list for good. The underlying commits remain recoverable by oid until git collects them - there will be no further prompt.
stash.dropRecoverHint: Dropped oids are written to the audit history and can be recovered until git collects them.
stash.clearImpact: All {{count}} stashes will be dropped and cannot be restored from this list.
stash.branchTitle: Create a branch from this stash
stash.branchHint: The branch starts at the stash's base and applies its contents - the regular way out of an 'apply conflict', and it cannot conflict with your worktree.
stash.branchImpact: Creates a new branch and switches to it; the current branch and the rest of your worktree are untouched.

historyOps.title: Commit actions
historyOps.pickHint: Select a commit in the graph to see the actions available for it.

reflog.title: Recent ref movements (reflog)
reflog.recoverHint: Creates a new branch at {{oid}}: no existing branch moves and nothing is checked out.
reflog.recoverImpact: Only a new branch pointing at that commit is created; the current branch, the index and the worktree are untouched.

resetPlan.title: Reset plan ({{mode}})
resetPlan.impact: {{count}} of the {{total}} commits being discarded exist nowhere but this machine - afterwards only a snapshot or the reflog can bring them back.
resetPlan.description: Resets to "{{subject}}", discarding the {{discarded}} commits after it.
resetPlan.lostStaged: Staged changes will be discarded: {{count}} files.
resetPlan.lostWorktree: Worktree changes will be discarded: {{count}} files.
resetPlan.confirmationPrompt: Type "{{word}}" to confirm (this is the last confirmation)

history.title: History
history.description: Browse the commit graph: branches, merges and refs at a glance.
